subject: Request: Subprocessor roster & evidence for EU procurement review
messages:
From: Evelyn Clarke <evelyn.clarke@therahealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
Cc: procurement@therahealth.com
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask: Subprocessor list + evidence for procurement packet

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this. We're preparing the vendor packet for our EU procurement committee and need a consolidated subprocessor roster plus the most recent SOC 2 and SIG/CAIQ artifacts we can reference. High-level ask: a CSV with subprocessor name, service provided, data residency, encryption responsibility (yes/no), and whether a DPA or onshore exception exists.

If you can also attach the latest SOC 2 Type II report and an annotated SIG-Lite mapping showing where Redwood's controls align to our requirements, that would speed our review. Target deadline is 2026-10-08 COB.

Appreciate anything you can share ahead of the formal packet — two-page summary is also fine if there are redaction constraints.

Best,
Evelyn
Procurement Lead, TheraHealth

---
Note: we will need an NDA or protected link for any redacted evidence.
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
To: Evelyn Clarke <evelyn.clarke@therahealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com, logan_wright@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: Subprocessor list + evidence for procurement packet

Hi Evelyn — thanks for outlining the needs and the timeline. We're happy to support TheraHealth's procurement review. Quick notes:

- We'll provide a CSV roster with the columns you listed (name, service, residency, encryption, DPA/onshore-exception).
- SOC 2 Type II (full report) is available for customers under NDA; we can share via a protected Drive link or a secure portal.
- We maintain an annotated SIG-Lite export aligned to the SIG questionnaire — we'll provide a version flagged for EU residency controls.

I'm looping in Laura (Security Evidence) and Logan (Privacy & Legal) to confirm redaction boundaries and DPA status for certain subprocessors. Laura/Logan — can you confirm whether we should: 1) include vendor contact info in the CSV; 2) mark any subprocessors as "onshore exception" (we have a few EU-residency partners and a couple of US-based analytics providers that require note).

We aim to have a preliminary package to you by 2026-10-06 EOD and the guarded evidence links by 2026-10-07. If you need anything faster (e.g., the roster only), say so and we'll prioritize.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: Subprocessor list + evidence for procurement packet

Neha,

Quick answers to your asks:

1) Vendor contact info: include only vendor name and point-of-contact role (e.g., "Acme Storage — Account Security Lead") — avoid personal emails in the public roster. Procurement can request full contact details via controlled channel if needed.

2) Onshore exceptions: marking policy — add column "residency_note" with values: EU-resident | US-resident (DPA in place) | Onshore-exception-requested. Current known items:
- VaultCorp (EU-resident) — no exception
- AnalyticsLab (US-resident) — DPA signed, data pseudonymized; mark as US-resident
- StreamBatch (US-resident) — customer-specific onshore exception historically requested; flag as "Onshore-exception-requested" and include comment "controls: restricted KV caching; PII not stored persistently"

3) SOC 2: attach the SOC 2 attestation (redacted) via protected Drive link; full report will require a signed NDA. I can prepare an executive summary for procurement with the auditor opinion and scope.

I'll prepare the CSV and annotated SIG-Lite worksheet and upload to the secure folder. Marissa, can you confirm whether any subprocessor entries must be excluded due to export-control or contractual embargo?

Laura
Director, Security Evidence
From: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: Subprocessor list + evidence for procurement packet

Laura / Neha — answered in-line:

- Export-control / embargo: checked the roster; no subprocessors require removal for TheraHealth's EU procurement packet. A few experimental partners are under NDA and we should flag them as "contact for details" rather than listing specifics.
- Attachments: I'm uploading three files to the secure folder now: Redwood_SUBPROCESSOR_ROSTER_2026.csv, SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2025.pdf (redacted summary version), SIG-Lite_annotated_thera.xlsx. Links below are protected; Evelyn, I'll send the secure links to the procurement inbox as soon as you confirm your preferred access method (Drive link with restricted domain or one-time download token).

Files: Redwood_SUBPROCESSOR_ROSTER_2026.csv (columns: vendor,service,residency,encryption_responsibility,dpa_status,residency_note,control_comments)
SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2025.pdf (executive summary, auditor opinion, control exceptions — redacted per policy)
SIG-Lite_annotated_thera.xlsx (SIG control rows + Redwood evidence pointers and attachments ids)

Marissa Cole
Security Program Manager

Evelyn / TheraHealth procurement team —

Thanks for your patience. Per your request, attached/provided in the secure folder:

- Redwood_SUBPROCESSOR_ROSTER_2026.csv (CSV roster; vendor contact roles only; residency notes and DPA status included)
- SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2025.pdf (redacted executive report)
- SIG-Lite_annotated_thera.xlsx (annotated mapping against SIG-Lite controls; rows we believe are relevant to EU data residency are flagged)

1) Google Drive link restricted to *@therahealth.com (recommended)
2) One-time secure download token (valid 72 hours)
3) We can execute a short mutual NDA and provide the full SOC 2 report and unredacted SIG attachments.

- All production-hosting subprocessors handling EU user data are EU-resident or covered by a DPA that includes standard SCCs.
- No subprocessors with export-control restrictions prevent us from sharing redacted evidence.
- A small set of analytics partners operate from the US with pseudonymization controls; these are flagged in "residency_note" in the CSV.

Evelyn — which access option do you prefer?

Best regards,
Neha Kapoor
